ceiling_and_reachable_line.source: docs/pivot/upper-bound-result.md and docs/pivot/evidence/upper-bound/score.json (#635, PR #703), taken unchanged: the declaration metadata/upper_bound_635.json, its inputs, settings and seeds; the fits are rerun by `scripts/upper_bound_635.py fit` and their per-day laws are scored here on the same days
ceiling_and_reachable_line.ceiling: the cross-fitted gradient-boosted fit, 'ceiling gbm' of H2 (ten contiguous blocks per lead, the walk-forward's embargo before the block and its mirror after it), at its generous settings
ceiling_and_reachable_line.reachable: the walk-forward gradient-boosted fit, 'reachable gbm' of H2 (refit every 21 scored days on the rows public at the block's first decision instant, 250 training rows at least)
ceiling_and_reachable_line.family: the gradient-boosted family in both cases (the better of the two families by H2's rule, in every cell of H2's tables); the ridge fits are not used
ceiling_and_reachable_line.check: the rerun must reproduce H2's recorded skills against B1 on the walk-forward ordinary days (reachable gbm +0.192, ceiling gbm +0.162) to three decimals, or the score refuses to read them as H2's

scale.metric: grid CRPS in bp (twice the mean pinball loss over the 23 levels of protocol v1), averaged over leads 1 to 5, one number per decision day (repo_model.scoring_protocol.day_scores)
scale.benchmark: B1, as-of persistence (repo_model.protocol_benchmarks.b1_forecast); B2, calendar climatology, reported beside it
scale.skill: (mean S(B1) - mean S(forecast)) / mean S(B1); positive favours the forecast
scale.window: the walk-forward decision days of H2 (the first is 2019-07-31), 1,598 of them; the candidate's own walk starts earlier and is restricted to these days; a decision day with no B2 is left out of every window
scale.headline_pool: ordinary targets (a decision day is scored on those of its five targets that are not risk dates), as in H2; the pool of all targets is reported beside it, as in #634
scale.interval: the stationary bootstrap of the protocol: mean block 10, one draw shared by every pair (seed 758), the 5th to 95th percentile of the paired draws as the 90% interval (H2's form), and the one-sided 95% lower bound of the mean daily difference; 10,000 draws on the pooled cells, 2,000 on the splits (H2's)

headroom.definition: headroom = skill(ceiling gbm against B1) - skill(candidate against B1), in skill points; the paired draws of the two skills share one resample, so the interval is the 5th to 95th percentile of the draw-wise difference. The same gap is also given relative to the candidate (skill of the ceiling against the candidate's own scores), and the gap to the reachable line the same way. Positive headroom means the ceiling is ahead of the candidate.
splits: pressure-day type of the target day: ordinary, month_end, quarter_end, tax_date (splits.reporting_day_type)
the upper tail: upper-tail twCRPS with weight 1{y > 0 bp} (all targets, and ordinary targets)
headroom.note: a split with fewer than 30 decision days is reported as too thin and read as 'not shown'; the splits are reported beside the pooled figure, never alone, and are not a pass requirement (protocol v1 section 7)

reading_rule.headroom_shown: the 90% interval of the headroom has a lower end above 0; otherwise 'not shown'. It is a one-sided 95% reading with no adjustment for the number of splits, and a development reading, never a verdict.

recommendation.continue model work: headroom is shown pooled on ordinary targets, or in at least one regime, day type or the upper tail with at least 30 decision days; the recommendation then names where, by split
recommendation.stop at the best available candidate: headroom is shown nowhere; the next step is step 5 (choose the primary from development by the protocol score alone)

reading_rule.one_recommendation: the result page ends with exactly one of the two, the trade-off in one line, and a marked question for Eleonora; no registration, no protocol change
reading_rule.cap: if the candidate is ahead of the ceiling, the headroom is negative and is read as 'not shown'; that is reported plainly, because the ceiling is a cross-fitted fit and not a bound on what a forecast could do
reading_rule.best_candidate: the one of the two candidates with the lower mean grid CRPS on the pooled ordinary-target cell of the window; the recommendation is read on it and the other is shown beside it. The cells read: pooled (ordinary targets and all targets), each regime, each day type, and the upper-tail twCRPS pooled (all targets and ordinary targets)
